newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa runs into technicals, trims gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa runs into technicals, trims gains.

text.p: London cocoa futures stood firmer on Wednesday but the technical rally on speculative short covering stalled as New York ran out of fuel, traders said.
"People were looking for follow-through. But we just saw the upward move on the opening call," said one trader.

Benchmark March cocoa bumped into resistance at around the session high of 943 stg where it saw a chain of trade and some origin sales. It closed in the middle of the day's range at 940 stg a tonne, up three.
Most of the day's activity of 9,005 lots consisted of Dec/March switches which traded up to 42 stg in the session.
"You're looking purely at Dec liquidation," said the trader.
December enters its first notice day on Monday and is likely to remain under pressure for the rest of the week as open interest shrinks at a fast pace and New York will close for Thanksgiving.
Traders and technical analysts reckoned that the market had potential to extend gains, but short-term attempts would be resisted.
"There is an opportunity to move up to 962 but at the moment it feels a little too much," said one trader.
A sizeable 1,500 lots of AAs were recorded on Wednesday and the Dec/May switch traded at 57 stg, traders said.

General Cocoa "guesstimated" Ivorian arrivals by November 16 at 195,000 tonnes and sales of the 1996/97 harvest at 750,000 tonnes so far, including a porton of price-fixing completed against the long-term cocoabean contract with a leading trade house and cocoa products contracts.
Traders said the report was seen bullish for the market.
"If you think the crop is going to be one million tonnes, they are not going to be in a great rush to sell," said one.
